thread:
maria: Hey team — seeing a weird auth regression after a customer upgraded to our latest node SDK and bundled their app with Next 13 + webpack. They suddenly get 401s from the API only in production builds, local dev works fine.

devon-support: Ugh, do we have a repro? Which SDK version and how are they importing?

maria: SDK @redwood/inference@0.12.3. Their package.json is type: "module" and they import like `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'`. It works during `next dev` but after `next build && next start` requests are missing the Authorization header (server-side).

kevin-eng-runtime: Missing header from server builds often means something is swapping/faking fetch or the bundler replaced our node entry with a browser shim. Can you paste their package.json exports?

maria: They don't have an explicit exports map. Minimal snippet: ```json
{
  "name": "customer-app",
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/inference": "0.12.3",
    "next": "13.x"
  }
}
```

samir-devex: Without exports map our package has dual entry points but some bundlers will pick the `browser`/`module` field which can pull in a ESM/browser build that expects global fetch behavior, causing edge-case auth stripping if a fetch polyfill is used. Is the customer using any fetch polyfills (node-fetch, unfetch)?

maria: They do have `isomorphic-fetch` in the dependency tree (brought in by another lib).

kevin-eng-runtime: That fits. In server-builds Next may tree-shake and resolve to our browser ESM entry which relies on `globalThis.fetch` semantics. If a polyfill installed earlier mutates fetch and doesn't forward headers on internal redirects, Authorization can be lost. Two quick repro steps: 1) Force resolution to server entry by creating an exports map or import our explicit node entry: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference/dist/node/index.js'` 2) Remove the fetch polyfill.

maria: Quick test: I asked them to try `require('@redwood/inference').default` fallback and they said that fixed the 401 in prod build. So this is a resolver/runtime mismatch.

devon-support: Is this an SDK packaging bug we should fix (exports map / clearer docs)? Or do we just document the workaround?

kevin-eng-runtime: We should ship a compatibility entry: add an explicit `exports` map in the package that points "./package.json": "./package.json", "import": "./dist/node/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/node/index.cjs" (example). Also ensure `types` points to the node types. That will make bundlers pick the server entry on SSR builds.

samir-devex: Agreed. Short-term: add a note to the troubleshooting docs for Next/webpack about fetch polyfills and how to force node entry. Long-term: patch release that updates package exports + add check in the bundler compatibility matrix.

maria: I'll send repro steps back to the customer: 1) remove isomorphic-fetch or move it to devDep 2) pin import to `@redwood/inference/dist/node` 3) try SDK 0.12.4-canary when we cut it.

kevin-eng-runtime: Also add a guard in the SDK to detect when `globalThis.fetch` looks like a shim and log a warning with helpful text (so users know why auth headers might be stripped).

deploy-bot: deploy started: patch/docs-next-bundler-compat -> staging (CI #4221) :rocket:

maria: Thanks — assigning to @samir-devex and @kevin-eng-runtime to own the docs + packaging change. I'll keep the thread updated with customer verification. :thumbsup:
